quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of these will you NOT need to adjust?

options.text: Tire pressure
Suspension
Headlight
Brake light

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You must adjust tire pressure, suspension settings, and headlight position if needed.

questions.question: What happens when you ride on the far side of a lane behind another vehicle?

options.text: It is recommended because drivers will see you easily
It is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors and may not see you
It is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there
It is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors and may not see you
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: The center of the lane has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction
Avoid the entire center of the lane
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars build up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, there is usually enough traction. When it rains, the strip becomes slippery. You can ride on either side of the strip and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed
Avoid making sudden moves
Use only the front brake when stopping
Use both brakes when stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when stopping
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down or stop. Also reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges—these areas are extra slippery.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions
Only ride in the center of the lane so others see you
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Move around the lane based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ times more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two
Three
Six
Twenty

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?

options.text: Just your head
Your head and shoulders
Just your shoulders
Your entire body

questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to see where you are going. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it easily

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: What is a linked braking system?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either lever is used
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting
It connects the rear brake to a foot control
It connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either lever is used
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake, both brakes get braking pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader
In front of the group
At the rear of the group
Beside the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: As a rider, what should you NOT tell a passenger to do before a ride?

options.text: Get on after the engine is started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to board after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the handholds or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do on a long ride to prevent fatigue?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit daily riding distance.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To fight fatigue, dress for bad weather like wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day. Stop for a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. They cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When weight shifts to the front of your bike while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly add more pressure to the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Do nothing. Weight transfer does not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly add more pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: As weight moves forward to the front tire while braking, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips again. Then re-apply the brake.

questions.question: When it is raining, what is the best place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Off the road until the rain stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
At a faster speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to chase the group. It also lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, how should you position your body?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What helps reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially important in areas where hazards might appear.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.
